title: Optimize CPU request path: reduce serialization, shard threadpools, and add thread pinning
author: Aisha Gupta
description: Motivation: CPU-side request handling was a dominant tail latency contributor for small/batched requests. This PR targets three pain points: (1) excessive serialization/deserialization copies when moving request metadata and KV cache payloads between network, scheduler, and inference threads; (2) global thread-pool contention (single pool handling both network IO, scheduling, and kernel prep) causing jitter under load; (3) lack of CPU core affinity causing cross-socket cache misses and suboptimal latency. Changes: implement zero-copy move semantics for request headers and KV cache slices across stages (Rust: Arc + Cow-based fast-paths), introduce sharded thread pools for network/scheduler/kernels with configurable shard counts, add optional per-shard CPU pinning with sensible defaults (one shard per hyperthread pair on each socket). Also added lightweight lock-free QoS queue for real-time small requests to avoid head-of-line blocking by large-batched prep jobs. Includes telemetry: new perf counters for serialization copies avoided, per-shard queue depths, and core-affinity mapping. Testing: microbenchmarks (latency P50/P95/P99) show 18% P95 reduction and 25% P99 reduction for 4-8 token requests in our perf lab; CPU utilization improves with fewer cross-thread wakeups. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag "cpu_request_path_opt" and default-off for Dedicated customers until validated in canaries. See Linear tickets ENG-3221 and ENG-3298 for context and perf lab results.

review_comments: Evan Park (2026-02-28): Nice end-to-end here. Can you quantify how many copies are avoided for a typical small request? Also confirm alignment with KV cache ownership semantics.

Aisha Gupta (2026-03-01): @Evan we measure ~2 full copies avoided for small chat turns (headers + small KV slice). KV cache now hands over Arc-backed slices so ownership is preserved; added unit tests (test_kv_zero_copy_ownership).

Diego Morales (2026-03-01): Thread-pinning changes look good. Suggest making pinning default off for cloud-hosted customers to avoid noisy-neighbor assumptions — config flag looks present, but add clear docs.
Aisha Gupta (2026-03-02): @Diego agreed, pinning default is false in config and docs updated in docs/runtime/perf_tuning.md. Added a note about Dedicated recommendations.
Priya Nair (2026-03-02): Can we add a guard to the QoS queue to avoid starvation of batch jobs? We should expose a tunable ratio.
Aisha Gupta (2026-03-02): Added a tunable 'replenish_ratio' with descriptive comment and a unit test to ensure batches progress.
